blocks.p: A two-way radio sends as well as receives. Walkie-talkies and the ham sets each have their own face in the *Radio* tab, and every knob and key on the face works. Figure 37-1 shows a ham set; a walkie-talkie is shown on the facing page.

caption: Figure 37-1
A ham set in the Radio tab.

blocks.p: On the ham set, the *CH* keys step through the channels and *MEM* is the memory key; hold it to name a channel. The red marker on the dial follows the frequency, and *RANGE* shows how far the set transmits.
The arrows at the top of the tab step from one radio within reach to the next. Between them is where the radio is, such as *Floor*.

marks.text: The red marker follows the frequency.
Range shows how far the set transmits.

blocks.p: Figure 37-2 shows a ValuTech walkie-talkie held in the main hand, in the *Radio* tab at the right and in full view at the left. On its face are *VOL - PWR* and *TUNE*, the display, the channel keys either side of *M*, and *PUSH TO TALK*; every one of them works.

caption: Figure 37-2
Full view, left, and the Radio tab, right.

blocks.p: To open full view, click the button at the right of the tab's header, or click the face. Full view shows the face on its own, with no window frame; drag it anywhere on the screen.

marks.text: The button at the right of the header opens full view. A click on the face does too.
Every knob and key on the face works: volume, tuning, channels, memory and push to talk.
Full view: the face on its own, with no window frame. Drag it anywhere.

sticky.text: Each radio gets its own face, and every knob works.
